items.event_title: TSMC August revenue jumps 53.3% to a record NT$514.8 billion as AI demand persists
items.news_summary: TSMC reported record August revenue of about NT$514.8 billion, up 53.3% year over year and 10.1% month over month, reinforcing that advanced-node AI demand remains exceptionally strong.
items.investor_materiality: Direct read-through to Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom and the wider AI accelerator/foundry supply chain; record revenue also supports TSMC pricing and capacity-expansion power.
items.selection_reason: One of the clearest fresh hard-data signals for the global AI semiconductor cycle.
items.source_quality_note: Reuters-syndicated report; figures also align with TSMC monthly-revenue reporting framework.

items.entity: China AI chip / HBM supply chain
items.event_title: Chinese AI chipmakers raise prices as HBM shortage bites
items.news_summary: Reuters reported Huawei, Cambricon, MetaX and Iluvatar CoreX are raising AI accelerator prices as advanced HBM remains scarce and expensive under export restrictions; Huawei's newer cards have seen large price increases.
items.investor_materiality: Directly affects the competitive economics of Nvidia alternatives in China and strengthens the strategic value of HBM suppliers SK Hynix, Samsung and Micron.
items.selection_reason: Combines China AI-chip competition, U.S. export controls and the global memory bottleneck in one identifiable catalyst.
items.source_quality_note: Reuters exclusive based on industry sources.

items.entity: South Korea U.S. AI infrastructure investment
items.event_title: South Korea nears more than $100 billion U.S. investment package centered on AI infrastructure and power
items.news_summary: Reuters, citing the Wall Street Journal, reported South Korea is nearing an agreement for more than $100 billion in U.S. investments that could include up to eight nuclear reactors and a Texas gas plant supporting AI data centers.
items.investor_materiality: Major potential tailwind for U.S. AI data centers, power equipment, nuclear supply chains and Korean semiconductor-linked capital spending.
items.selection_reason: The scale is unusually large and directly connects geopolitics, tariffs, power infrastructure and AI capex.
items.source_quality_note: Reuters report citing WSJ; final terms are still under negotiation, so amounts and project scope should be treated as proposed.
